墨西哥維瑞拉琴是十九世紀墨西哥的五弦吉他類弦樂器，琴身小巧、胴部較深，琴背呈凸形: The vihuela mexicana is a five-string guitar-family chordophone of nineteenth-century Mexico: a small body, deeper sides and a convex back, built much like the guitarrón and also resembling the Canary Island timple. It is usually played in mariachi bands, strung with nylon and tuned re-entrant to sound higher, so that it pairs high against the Spanish guitar. It is played mostly by strumming with the fingernails or with a finger pick, to produce a clear, full chordal rhythm.
墨西哥維瑞拉琴為五弦撥弦樂器，第三、四、五弦較吉他高八度，音色偏高而具男高音感。: The vihuela mexicana is a five-string plucked instrument; its third, fourth and fifth strings lie an octave above the guitar's, so its timbre is high and has a tenor quality. Its volume and timbre depend on string gauge, the order in which the strings are fitted and where you pluck: plucking between the soundhole and the point where the fretboard meets the body gives a soft or a forceful rhythmic sound. Plucking with all the fingernails gives full, clear chords; using a finger pick on the index or middle finger, with the ring finger free, is brighter. It differs from the historical Spanish vihuela and is closer to the Canary Island timple, since both have five strings and a convex back; in the mariachi it complements the Spanish guitar, one high and one low.
墨西哥維瑞拉琴琴身採用優質木材製成共鳴箱，通常選用雲杉或其他共鳴木作為面板，背板: The body of the vihuela mexicana is made of good wood forming the soundbox, usually spruce or another resonant wood for the top and rosewood or another hardwood for the back and sides. The neck is a solid wood, and the fretboard is mostly ebony or another dark hardwood. The strings are metal or nylon: metal gives a bright timbre, nylon a gentler one. The joint between peghead and body uses fine joinery, and some finely made instruments have metal machine heads and decorative fittings.
墨西哥維瑞拉琴起源於西班牙，為五弦撥弦樂器。十六世紀西班牙征服者將其帶入墨西哥，: The vihuela mexicana originated in Spain as a five-string plucked instrument. Sixteenth-century Spanish conquerors brought it to Mexico, and over several centuries of local adaptation it gradually took on features of Indigenous music culture. In the colonial period it became an important part of Mexican folk music, and was widely used especially in rural areas.
維瑞拉琴主要流行於墨西哥西部地區，特別是哈利斯科州和納亞里特州，成為民間樂隊與傳: The vihuela is found mainly in western Mexico, especially in Jalisco and Nayarit, where it is a standard instrument of the folk band and of traditional music. In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, as Mexican national feeling grew, the vihuela gained wider attention and esteem. Today it has become a symbol of Mexican cultural identity, still plays an important part in traditional performance and folk events, and has spread to other parts of Latin America through band line-ups.
